meta.title: Digital Exhibition — Headless Migration
meta.subtitle: Cloudflare front-end + slimmed WordPress backend
meta.client: TU/e — Built Environment, Digital Exhibition platform
meta.repoBackend: backend (WordPress, LAMP on TU/e Flask server)
meta.author: marco@tech-paw.com
meta.summary: Move Digital Exhibition to a headless architecture: a Nuxt 3 / Vue / Tailwind front-end on Cloudflare Pages that consumes the existing WordPress REST API through a server proxy, while the WordPress install on the TU/e server is stripped back to a lean content API. Media moves to Cloudflare R2, transactional mail moves to Brevo, and SEO becomes a first-class concern of the front-end instead of the WP theme. The WordPress backend (wp-content) is put under Git version control with a reviewed staging→production deploy pipeline (GitHub Actions over SSH), so files are changed, checked on staging, and pushed to production only when they pass.

workstreams.name: Cloudflare front-end (Nuxt)
workstreams.goal: A production Nuxt 3 front-end on Cloudflare Pages that renders the whole Digital Exhibition from the WordPress REST API, with no upstream host or CORS exposed to the browser.
workstreams.context: Already scaffolded in frontend/digital-exhibition: Nuxt 3.14, @nuxtjs/tailwindcss, hybrid rendering (≈15 pre-rendered shell routes, entries rendered on-demand by the Pages Worker and edge-cached SWR 3600s).

workstreams.name: Slim the TU/e WordPress server
workstreams.goal: Reduce the WordPress install on the TU/e (Flask-hosted) LAMP box to what a content API actually needs — no front-end theme rendering weight, no dead code.
workstreams.context: backend/ holds a full WP core + wp-content. The front-end no longer needs WP to render pages for humans, only JSON (plus the Elementor single-region fallback).

tasks.title: Inventory the server: disk, plugins, themes, uploads size
tasks.notes: du -sh wp-content/*, list active vs inactive plugins, DB size, PHP version.

tasks.title: Identify 'useless folder' — the redundant LAMP-stack backend dir
tasks.notes: User flagged a leftover folder used for a local LAMP backend of WP. Confirm it is not referenced by wp-config.php / .htaccess, back it up, remove it.

tasks.title: Remove unused themes, keep one lightweight fallback
tasks.notes: Done on the local backend — chique, chique-pro, twentytwentyfive removed; only active theme 'digital' kept. Mirror on staging/prod when they exist.

tasks.title: Deactivate + delete confirmed-unused plugins
tasks.notes: Driven by workstream 3 audit. Candidates: wordpress-importer, better-search-replace, duplicate-page, regenerate-thumbnails, show-current-template (keep only while migrating).

tasks.title: Lock down / disable front-end rendering paths not needed by REST
tasks.notes: xmlrpc, comments endpoints, author archives, feeds — disable what the front-end never calls. Note: disable-wp-rest-api plugin is installed; must NOT block the endpoints the proxy needs.

tasks.title: Set object/opcode cache + sane PHP limits for API-only load
tasks.notes: Opcache on, lower memory ceilings, WP-Cron via system cron.

tasks.title: Document the final server layout in backend/README
tasks.notes: What runs, why, how to restore, who owns it at TU/e.

workstreams.name: WordPress audit & plugin rationalisation
workstreams.goal: Decide, plugin by plugin, what stays, what is replaced, and what is removed — without touching the two heavy dependencies the content genuinely relies on.
workstreams.context: Installed plugins: advanced-custom-fields-pro, better-search-replace, custom_dashboard, dflip, disable-wp-rest-api, duplicate-page, elementor, elementor-pro, figuro-folder, filebird-pro, header-footer-elementor, post-grid-elementor-addon, post-type-switcher, regenerate-thumbnails, show-current-template, wordpress-importer, wordpress-seo, wp-mail-smtp.

tasks.title: FileBird Pro → open replacement
tasks.notes: Media-library folder organisation. Pro licence swapped out. figuro-folder present as the free alternative — verify folder assignments survived.

tasks.title: DearFlip (dflip) → replacement / self-host
tasks.notes: PDF flipbook. Options: (a) drop the WP plugin, ship a front-end flipbook (own useDflip against a JS lib served from the front-end), (b) keep dflip only as an asset host, (c) plain PDF viewer + R2 link. Front-end already has composables/useDflip.ts. Decide with 4.1 (PDFs on R2).

tasks.title: Keep — Advanced Custom Fields PRO (do not touch)
tasks.notes: Field data drives the REST payloads the front-end consumes. No change. Confirm ACF-to-REST exposure is on for the fields the front-end reads.

tasks.title: Keep — Elementor + Elementor Pro (do not touch)
tasks.notes: 2025–2026 batch of post/courses/seminars is authored in Elementor; content.rendered is empty for those and the front-end lifts elementor-location-single from the rendered page. Removing Elementor breaks that batch.

tasks.title: Decide — wp-toolkit
tasks.notes: wp-toolkit is an mu-plugin in this install (wp-content/mu-plugins/wp-toolkit*), not the Plesk panel. Evaluate for removal on the slimmed backend.

tasks.title: Decide — content audit plugin
tasks.notes: No 'audit content' plugin is installed under that name. If the user wants a one-off content inventory, do it with WP-CLI / a spreadsheet export, not a permanent plugin.

tasks.title: Decide — comments
tasks.notes: Digital Exhibition is a showcase; comments add spam surface and REST noise. Recommend: disable comments site-wide (setting + close on existing), no plugin needed.

tasks.title: Decide — WP Mail SMTP → Brevo
tasks.notes: wp-mail-smtp is installed. Two mail paths: (a) WP-originated mail (admin, password reset) — repoint wp-mail-smtp to Brevo SMTP; (b) front-end contact/newsletter — call the Brevo API directly from the Nuxt server (see 4.4). Long-term the front-end owns transactional mail.

tasks.title: Decide — custom_dashboard / show-current-template / post-type-switcher
tasks.notes: custom_dashboard: keep if editors rely on it. show-current-template: dev-only, remove for prod. post-type-switcher: keep only if content still being re-typed during migration, else remove.

tasks.title: Decide — header-footer-elementor / post-grid-elementor-addon
tasks.notes: Front-end renders its own header/footer (scraped nav in libs/navigation.ts) and its own grids. These matter only for the WP-rendered fallback pages — keep until 1.13 QA confirms the fallback never shows them.

tasks.title: Decide — Yoast SEO (wordpress-seo)
tasks.notes: Confirmed yoast_head_json is in the REST output and consumed by the front-end. Yoast now only stores per-entry meta; all rendering is front-end. Title templates still worth tidying in Yoast (some double up the site name).

tasks.title: Produce the final keep/replace/remove table
tasks.notes: Sign-off artefact — see pluginAudit below.

workstreams.name: Assets, domain, staging & mail on Cloudflare
workstreams.goal: Media served from Cloudflare R2, the domain on Cloudflare, a safe staging copy of the WordPress site, and Brevo handling SMTP.

tasks.title: Move images & PDFs to R2
tasks.notes: Sync wp-content/uploads to an R2 bucket; put it behind a Cloudflare custom domain (e.g. media.digitalexhibition…). Rewrite media URLs in REST responses at the proxy layer (server/api/wp/[...path].ts) so the front-end always points at R2. Keep WP uploads as the origin of record during migration.

tasks.title: Add the domain to Cloudflare
tasks.notes: digitalexhibition.arch.tue.nl is a TU/e subdomain — needs TU/e DNS/IT cooperation (likely a CNAME or a delegated zone, or a new apex like digitalexhibition.nl). Blocked on TU/e IT. Fallback: run the front-end on a *.pages.dev + a Cloudflare-owned domain first.

tasks.title: Stand up a staging environment of the current WP site
tasks.notes: Clone WP (files + DB) to a staging host, search-replace URLs. Front-end points WP_API_BASE at staging so migration work never touches production. This is the safe place to delete plugins/themes (workstreams 2 & 3).

tasks.title: Brevo for transactional mail from the front-end
tasks.notes: Front-end contact form built: components/ContactForm.vue + server/api/contact.post.ts (validation, honeypot, field errors) on /contact/ via PageView. Currently logs only — Brevo API call is a marked TODO(brevo) in the handler; runtimeConfig keys added (brevoApiKey, brevoListId, contactToEmail, contactFromEmail). Still: WP-side wp-mail-smtp → Brevo SMTP, Turnstile, newsletter endpoint.

tasks.title: R2 lifecycle / caching / cost check
tasks.notes: Cache-Control on R2 objects, Cloudflare cache rules, confirm egress stays in free tier, document the re-sync procedure for new uploads.

tasks.title: Cutover plan: DNS, cache purge, rollback
tasks.notes: Order of operations to point real traffic at the Pages front-end, with a documented rollback to the WP site.

workstreams.name: SEO on the front-end
workstreams.goal: The Nuxt front-end owns all discoverability: per-page meta, Open Graph, structured data, sitemap, robots — sourced from Yoast fields via REST.
workstreams.context: The front-end is currently noindex everywhere (robots.txt Disallow: /, meta robots, X-Robots-Tag via public/_headers). That must be lifted deliberately at cutover.

tasks.title: Per-route meta from yoast_head_json
tasks.notes: Implemented — utils/seo.ts maps yoast_head_json → title/description/canonical/OG/Twitter; composables/useSeo.ts wires it via useHead. Verified against /privacy-policy/, /contact/, entries.

tasks.title: Structured data (JSON-LD)
tasks.notes: Implemented — Yoast's schema @graph is passed through with WP-origin URLs rewritten to the public host; home feed emits a hand-written WebSite + Organization graph.

tasks.title: Dynamic sitemap.xml
tasks.notes: Implemented — server/routes/sitemap.xml.ts enumerates pages + archives + all entries from the proxy (161 URLs). 404s while not indexable.

tasks.title: Canonical strategy vs the WP domain
tasks.notes: utils/seo.rewriteOrigin() rewrites every WP URL (canonical/og:url/schema) to public.siteUrl. Final host decision still open (d2).

tasks.title: Lift noindex at cutover
tasks.notes: Gated behind NUXT_PUBLIC_INDEXABLE (default false): while false every route emits noindex + no JSON-LD + sitemap 404. Flip together with public/robots.txt and public/_headers (checklist added to both files).

tasks.title: Redirects for changed permalinks
tasks.notes: Cloudflare Pages _redirects / Bulk Redirects — not started.

tasks.title: Perf / Core Web Vitals pass + Search Console
tasks.notes: Lighthouse / CWV + Search Console — after cutover.

tasks.title: Social / link-preview cards (OG image on a served host)
tasks.notes: buildSeoHead now sends page URLs (canonical/og:url/JSON-LD) to the front-end host but keeps /wp-content media URLs on public.mediaUrl (the WP box now, R2 later) so og:image never 404s. og:image:secure_url/type/alt + twitter:image:alt added. public/robots.txt allow-lists facebookexternalhit / Twitterbot / LinkedInBot / Slackbot / WhatsApp / etc. so shared links render a card while search stays blocked by the noindex meta. Note: _headers is Pages-only — no effect on a *.workers.dev deploy.

workstreams.name: Backend version control & deploy
workstreams.goal: Put the WordPress backend (wp-content) under Git and ship changes through a reviewed staging→production pipeline instead of editing files on the live server.
workstreams.context: Today the TU/e box is edited in place with no history and no safe way back. The front-end already has its own Git repo; the backend needs the same, plus an automated deploy path (SSH/rsync or GitHub Actions).

tasks.title: Initialise a Git repo for wp-content
tasks.notes: Done — git repo initialised in backend/. .gitignore excludes wp-config.php (secrets), *.log, WP upgrade-temp dirs, compressx logs. wp-config.reference.php + README.md added.

tasks.title: Decide what version control tracks
tasks.notes: Tracked now = wp-content only (plugins, active theme 'digital', mu-plugins, maintenance). Untracked/git-ignored, kept on localhost: WP core (wp-admin, wp-includes, root files), wp-content/ngg. Deleted locally + repo: inactive themes (chique, chique-pro, twentytwentyfive), wp-content/uploads/* (→ R2, 4.1). 9,962 files tracked (was 13,830). Open: history still carries the old blobs in commit 35c6d25 — squash+force-push if the GitHub repo size must shrink. Plugin-code-vs-composer still d8.

tasks.title: Host the repo privately on GitHub
tasks.notes: Done — pushed to github.com/orso081980/digitalexhibition-backend (private), branch main, initial commit 35c6d25 (~13.8k files).

tasks.title: Build the staging → production deploy pipeline
tasks.notes: GitHub Actions: on merge to main, deploy wp-content to the TU/e server. Mechanism — SSH + rsync --delete of tracked paths (preferred, no Git on the server), or git pull over SSH (d9). Default to manual workflow_dispatch; enable auto-deploy once trusted. Deploy only after the change is verified on staging.

tasks.title: Server prep + SSH deploy key
tasks.notes: Restricted deploy user on the TU/e box; its public key added as a GitHub Actions secret, scoped to the deploy path. Pre-deploy step: tar backup of wp-content + a DB dump. Post-deploy: clear opcache, fix ownership for runtime dirs.

tasks.title: Rollback procedure
tasks.notes: Tag every deploy (deploy-YYYYMMDD-HHMM). Rollback = redeploy the previous tag, or restore the pre-deploy tar. Keep the last 5 backups on the server. Do one rollback drill before cutover.

tasks.title: Protect main + change-review flow
tasks.notes: Branch protection on main: PR required, no direct pushes. Loop = edit on staging or locally → PR → review → merge → (verified) deploy. This is the 'change when needed, push to production if everything is ok' flow the team asked for.

tasks.title: Document the backend Git + deploy workflow
tasks.notes: backend/README: repo layout, what is / isn't tracked, how to make a change, how a deploy runs, how to roll back, who holds the deploy key. State that direct edits on the production server are frozen once the pipeline is live.

decisions.question: DearFlip: front-end flipbook library, or plain PDF viewer + R2 download?
decisions.recommendation: Front-end flipbook lib (e.g. a self-hosted viewer) so the WP plugin can be removed and PDFs live only on R2.

decisions.question: Does the front-end domain replace digitalexhibition.arch.tue.nl, or run alongside it?
decisions.recommendation: Replace it at cutover; keep the WP host reachable only as the private API origin (staging-style).

decisions.question: Can TU/e IT delegate DNS / add a CNAME for the arch.tue.nl subdomain to Cloudflare?
decisions.recommendation: Open the ticket on Day 1; have a *.pages.dev fallback.

decisions.question: What is 'wp-toolkit' — the Plesk hosting panel, or something else?
decisions.recommendation: RESOLVED: wp-toolkit here is a local mu-plugin (wp-content/mu-plugins/wp-toolkit.php + /wp-toolkit), NOT Plesk. Review whether it's needed on the API-only backend; likely removable.

decisions.question: Do editors actually use custom_dashboard and duplicate-page?
decisions.recommendation: Ask the editorial team before removing.

decisions.question: Keep comments anywhere on the platform?
decisions.recommendation: No — disable site-wide, close existing threads.

decisions.question: Brevo: SMTP relay only, or also newsletter/contact lists via API?
decisions.recommendation: Both — SMTP for WP mail, API + Turnstile for the front-end forms.

decisions.question: Backend plugins/themes: commit the code into Git as-is, or manage them via a composer.json / wp-cli manifest?
decisions.recommendation: Commit as-is for the timebox — simplest, no build step on deploy. Revisit a composer / WPackagist manifest later so premium plugin binaries aren't in Git.

decisions.question: Deploy mechanism: SSH + rsync from GitHub Actions, or git pull on the server?
decisions.recommendation: rsync --delete over SSH — no Git needed on the TU/e box, works with an old server toolchain, and the server tree can't drift from main.

decisions.question: Archiprix entries: the archiprix_category taxonomy only has Bachelor/Master (Master used by 3 of 20 entries); Archiprix is graduation-level by definition.
decisions.recommendation: Editorial: either drop archiprix_category entirely (redundant — all are graduation projects) or rename 'Master' → 'Graduation' and tag all 20 consistently. Front-end can meanwhile hide the archiprix category badge/tabs.

risks.risk: TU/e IT is slow to delegate DNS
risks.mitigation: Ticket on Day 1; ship on *.pages.dev first, swap the domain later.

risks.risk: disable-wp-rest-api blocks an endpoint the proxy needs
risks.mitigation: Test every proxied path against staging before touching prod; keep an allow-list.

risks.risk: Removing Elementor add-ons breaks the WP-rendered fallback for the 2025–2026 batch
risks.mitigation: Keep header-footer-elementor + post-grid addon until QA (1.13) proves the fallback is clean.

risks.risk: Media URL rewrite misses some field, front-end 404s images
risks.mitigation: Rewrite centrally at the proxy; keep WP uploads live as origin during migration.

risks.risk: noindex left on after cutover — front-end never gets indexed
risks.mitigation: 5.5 is an explicit gated checklist item on Day 5.
P2 tasks (JSON-LD, R2 lifecycle, CWV polish) can land the following week without blocking cutover.

risks.risk: Automated deploy overwrites an out-of-band change made directly on the production server
risks.mitigation: rsync --delete scoped to tracked paths only; pre-deploy backup; freeze direct server edits once the pipeline is live (stated in 6.8).

risks.risk: SSH deploy key is leaked or over-privileged
risks.mitigation: Dedicated restricted deploy user, key scoped to the deploy path, stored only as a GitHub encrypted secret, rotated at handover.

risks.risk: Once NUXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL is set, og:image could be rewritten to a host that has no /wp-content/
risks.mitigation: Fixed — media URLs rewrite to public.mediaUrl (WP box / R2), not the front-end host. Verified in dev.

architecture.before: Browser → WordPress (Elementor theme renders HTML) on TU/e LAMP box. Media, mail, SEO all inside WP.
architecture.after: Browser → Cloudflare Pages (Nuxt SSR/SSG, edge-cached) → /api/wp proxy → WordPress REST API (staging-style, API-only). Media → Cloudflare R2. Mail → Brevo. SEO owned by Nuxt. Backend file changes ship via Git + GitHub Actions (SSH/rsync) after passing on staging.
